proof:
Source: parent proof step 3, case n = 1 ("H⁰ is the counting measure, so θ ≥ 1 on M₀ and, by (MR), M_G(∂T) = Σ_{x∈M₀∩G}θ(x); by (VO) this vanishes for open G disjoint from spt ∂T, so M₀ ⊆ spt ∂T, and M₀ is finite (local integrability on the compact set spt ∂T). As in degree 0 the orientation is ±⟨·⟩ … so ∂T(g) = Σ m_i⟨g(x_i)⟩"), stated for an arbitrary compactly supported integer multiplicity 0-current S.
1. Let R = (M₀, θ, ζ) be an IMRep of S in ℝ^P (degree 0). H⁰ := μHE[0] equals μH[0] (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero), so H⁰({x}) = 1 for every x (hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Hence H⁰(t) = #t for every finite set t (sum_measure_singleton).
2. Carrier points have positive mass: for x ∈ M₀, R.measure({x}) = ∫⁻_{{x}} θ dH⁰ = θ(x)H⁰({x}) = θ(x) ≥ 1 (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, lintegral_singleton, field mult_pos).
3. M₀ ⊆ spt S. Let G := ℝ^P ∖ spt S; it is the zero region of S, a union of open sets, hence open. Every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ G has tsupport disjoint from spt S, so S(ω) = 0 by (VO); hence M_G(S) = 0. By (MR) (U = ℝ^P, W = G open), R.measure(G) = M_G(S) = 0. If x ∈ M₀ ∩ G, then R.measure({x}) ≤ R.measure(G) = 0, contradicting step 2. So M₀ ⊆ spt S.
4. M₀ is finite. By the field locallyIntegrable_mult for the compact set spt S and step 3, ∫⁻_{M₀} θ dH⁰ < ∞. If M₀ were infinite, then for every N ∈ ℕ there is a finite t ⊆ M₀ with #t = N (Set.Infinite.exists_subset_card_eq), and N = H⁰(t) = ∫⁻_t 1 dH⁰ ≤ ∫⁻_{M₀} 1 dH⁰ ≤ ∫⁻_{M₀} θ dH⁰ (θ ≥ 1 on M₀); so ∫⁻_{M₀} θ dH⁰ = ∞, a contradiction. Let F be the finite set M₀.
5. The orientation is ±⟨·⟩ at every carrier point. Let B be the set of x for which no subspace Q satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M₀ x Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (ζ(x)) Q. The field orients says H⁰(B ∩ M₀) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply' for the measurable M₀). Since singletons have H⁰-measure 1, B ∩ M₀ = ∅. So for x ∈ M₀ there are Q and an orthonormal τ : Fin 0 → ℝ^P with ζ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α or ζ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α; as Fin 0 is empty, τ is the empty tuple ⟨⟩. Hence ζ(x)(α) = s(x)·α(⟨⟩) with s(x) ∈ {1, −1}.
6. Formula. For a test 0-form g, S(g) = R.action(g) = ∫_{M₀} θ(x)ζ(x)(g(x)) dH⁰(x). The integrand is integrable on the finite set M₀, each singleton having finite measure (integrableOn_singleton_iff, integrableOn_finset_iUnion), so ∫_{M₀} h dH⁰ = Σ_{x∈F} H⁰({x})·h(x) = Σ_{x∈F} h(x) (setIntegral_finset). With step 5, S(g) = Σ_{x∈F} s(x)θ(x)·g(x)⟨⟩. Put m(x) := s(x)θ(x) ∈ ℤ. By step 3, F = M₀ ⊆ spt S. ∎
key_steps: μHE[0] gives mass 1 to every point, so every carrier point has positive R.measure.
(VO) gives M_{ℝ^P∖spt S}(S) = 0, so by (MR) the carrier lies in spt S.
Local integrability of θ ≥ 1 on the compact spt S makes the carrier finite.
The a.e. orientation condition holds at every carrier point, so ζ(x) = ±⟨·⟩.
The integral over the finite carrier is the finite sum S(g) = Σ ±θ(x)g(x)⟨⟩.
